layers.file: File:Female Mahogany Jerusalem Cricket Eaton LACO.oga

species: Real recording of a female mahogany Jerusalem cricket (Ammopelmatus) drumming her abdomen on the ground to attract a mate, used for the weta: no free recording of a weta exists, and Jerusalem crickets are close relatives of weta in the same insect superfamily (Stenopelmatoidea); some weta also drum this way
note: Recording by Dr. David Weissman (California Academy of Sciences), provided by Dr. Amy Vandergast (U.S. Geological Survey). The 70 Hz high-pass removes measured low-frequency background rumble between the drum rolls.
